newsitem.title: USA: AMR, BA, USAir must produce documents - court.
newsitem.headline: AMR, BA, USAir must produce documents - court.

text.p: AMR Corp, British Airways Plc (BA) and USAir Group Inc -- mired in a legal battle over the proposed alliance between BA and AMR's American Airlines -- must provide their opponents with certain documents, a U.S. federal judge said on Tuesday.

As part of the "discovery" process, all three airlines must produce copies of documents that were already given to the U.S. Department of Justice, which is reviewing the proposed agreement between BA and American, the court said.
The airlines also said they needed direction from the court before releasing all the documents requested by USAir.
U.S. District Court Judge Miriam Cedarbaum ruled that the airlines' must allow legal counsel for the opposing companies to review documents that are relevant to the case.

In July, USAir sued British Airways and American, saying their proposed marketing alliance undermined an existing pact between USAir and BA and would allow BA and American to monopolize air travel between the United States and Britain.
USAir plans to end its code-sharing pact with BA on March 29.
BA and American contend that their proposed alliance, which is contingent on a new Anglo-American air treaty, would not inhibit competition.
